title: LabSecurityConfig: the lab SecurityFilterChain
excerpt:
@Bean
    @Order(1)
    public SecurityFilterChain labSecureFilterChain(HttpSecurity http, LabJwtService lab,
                                                    DatabaseBackedJwtAuthenticationConverter converter,
                                                    RestAuthenticationEntryPoint authenticationEntryPoint,
                                                    RestAccessDeniedHandler accessDeniedHandler) throws Exception {
        http
                .securityMatcher("/api/lab/secure/**")
                .csrf(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable)
                .sessionManagement(session -> session.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS))
                .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
                        .requestMatchers("/api/lab/secure/admin-area").hasRole("ADMIN")
                        .requestMatchers("/api/lab/secure/teacher-area").hasAnyRole("TEACHER", "ADMIN")
                        .anyRequest().authenticated())
                .oauth2ResourceServer(oauth2 -> oauth2
                        .jwt(jwt -> jwt.decoder(lab.decoder()).jwtAuthenticationConverter(converter))
                        .authenticationEntryPoint(authenticationEntryPoint)
                        .accessDeniedHandler(accessDeniedHandler))
                .exceptionHandling(ex -> ex
                        .authenticationEntryPoint(authenticationEntryPoint)
                        .accessDeniedHandler(accessDeniedHandler));
        return http.build();

notes.text: This chain wins for its own paths; every other request still reaches the application's main chain.
This chain handles only /api/lab/secure/**.
Authorization rule: the ADMIN role is required.
Authorization rule: TEACHER or ADMIN.
Anything else under the lab path needs an authenticated caller.
A decoder INSTANCE for the lab key is passed directly, so no second JwtDecoder bean exists.
The application's own converter: the database lookup of role and enabled flag.
The application's own handler writes the 401.
The application's own handler writes the 403.

notes.text: A call needs a permit of the TARGET service. Without one it is rejected here and never reaches the handler.
UNAVAILABLE: the connection is refused, the request is never processed.
The request is lost: the caller times out although nothing was done.
The handler runs as ordinary Java code with its own local database transaction.

title: Bulkheads: bounded concurrency permits per service

notes.text: PER_SERVICE gives every service its own Semaphore, SHARED gives all services one.
A real, non-blocking Semaphore permit. null means the target is saturated.

title: Inventory: one local transaction decides the reservation

notes.text: The Inventory service commits its own short local transaction. No other service takes part in it.
Idempotent: asking again for the same order returns the existing reservation.
A guarded UPDATE (available >= quantity) takes the stock atomically; 0 rows changed means not enough.
A BUSINESS refusal: the service answered normally, it is not a failure of the service.

title: A run executes at most once: compare-and-set on its state

notes.text: A finished run returns its stored result and executes nothing.
The database decides which concurrent request wins the move CREATED to EXECUTING; the others get the stored result or a 409.

title: A service can register only its own operations

notes.text: Another service's contract operation cannot be implemented or hijacked from outside that service.

title: Every service gets its own connections and transaction manager

notes.text: One transaction manager per service, so a call from one service into another opens a second, independent transaction.

title: The monolith: one database transaction for the whole workflow

notes.text: One transaction covers users, products, stock, reservations and orders.
The stock is taken inside the same transaction as the order row.
An exception here rolls back EVERYTHING, including the stock already taken.

title: Order service: several synchronous calls, no shared transaction

notes.text: The order row is committed in the Order service's own local transaction, and it keeps a COPY of the unit price it was quoted.
A synchronous call: Inventory commits its own transaction; no transaction spans the two services.
After a timeout the order stays PENDING: this service cannot know whether the stock was reserved.
Lab fault injection: failing here leaves the reservation in place.
The event is published AFTER the commit, outside the transaction. This is not a transactional outbox.

title: The SIMULATED event channel: publish, then deliver as a separate step

notes.text: Appends to an in-memory list. The sender does not wait for any consumer. Not Kafka or RabbitMQ.
Delivery is its own step, made through the service bus and recorded as an EVENT call.

title: Idempotent consumer: the message id and the effect in one local transaction

notes.text: A message id handled before is ignored, so a duplicate delivery changes nothing.
The message id and the notification are written in ONE local transaction, so they cannot diverge.

title: The simulated gateway: authenticate, limit, route, translate

notes.text: Authentication comes first; a rejected request reaches no service.
A path with no route is answered by the gateway itself.

title: Fixed-window rate limiter on the simulated clock

notes.text: A new window starts once the simulated clock passes the end of the old one.
Over the limit: 429, without touching any service.
Counted per client id.

title: Registry resolve: healthy instances only, round-robin

notes.text: A name nobody registered is a business refusal, not a connection error.
Only instances that reported UP and whose heartbeat is fresh are candidates.
Every instance is unhealthy: the caller must handle this.
The round-robin position, kept per run.

title: Behaviour of ONE instance

notes.text: A behaviour set for one instance overrides the service-level one for calls aimed at that instance: how a single crashed instance is modelled.

title: The runtime ownership guard

notes.text: A statement that mentions a table the service does not own is refused before it reaches the driver. This is logical isolation enforced by lab code.

title: Transactional outbox: the order and its event row in ONE local transaction

notes.text: The outbox row is written in the SAME local transaction as the order row.
An exception here rolls back BOTH rows: this is a real database rollback, inside one local transaction.

title: The outbox relay: publish, then mark, as separate steps

notes.text: Publishes with the SAME message id as the outbox row, so a republication is recognisable as a duplicate.
A crash here leaves the row PENDING, so the next run publishes it again: delivery is at-least-once.
Marking the row PUBLISHED is a separate step after publishing.

title: Saga compensation, in reverse order

notes.text: The compensations of the completed steps run in reverse order.

notes.token: reversed by a new business operation
notes.text: A compensation is a new business operation (a release, a refund). It is not a database rollback.

title: Choreography: Inventory reacts to PaymentFailed

notes.text: Nothing coordinates this: Inventory reacts to an event by running its own compensation.
It then publishes StockReleased for the Order service to react to.

title: Circuit breaker: when OPEN becomes HALF_OPEN

notes.text: The breaker leaves OPEN exactly when the open duration has elapsed; the next call is the probe.

title: Bounded retries with deterministic backoff

notes.text: At most maxAttempts calls: retries are bounded.
The wait is spent on the simulated clock, never by sleeping, and counts as time of the enclosing span.
An open breaker refuses the call locally and it is not retried.

title: Idempotent charge: a repeated key returns the original payment

notes.text: A request with a key that was already used returns the original payment instead of charging again.
Two requests with the same key arriving together: the unique key lets exactly one insert through.

title: Correlation id and parent span

notes.text: A child call inherits the correlation id of its parent: this is the propagation.
When propagation is switched off the child starts an unrelated id and loses its parent link: the trace is broken.

title: The explicit expiry rule of the registry

notes.text: Fresh while the age is at most the TTL: healthy at exactly the TTL, stale from TTL + 1 ms.
